title: GPL compatibility
what_it_supports: Apache 2 software can be included in GPLv3 projects; GPLv3 software cannot be included in Apache projects (it would force distribution under GPLv3); the FSF has never considered the Apache License compatible with GPLv2 (patent termination and indemnification provisions).

title: Licensing and Compliance Lab: The most frequently asked Frequently Asked Questions
what_it_supports: Quotes the GPL FAQ: linking a program statically or dynamically with other modules makes a combined work based on it; licenses are compatible if there is a way to merge code under them.

title: Obligations of the LGPL
what_it_supports: Dynamic linking: application source may stay proprietary; static linking may bring the application under the LGPL; users must be able to relink; library source and license text must be provided. The page says it is not legal advice.

title: MPL 2.0 FAQ
what_it_supports: Q11: new files with no MPL code are not Modifications; Q12: copyleft applies to files containing MPL code; Q14: MPL can be combined with (L)GPL through a Larger Work under Section 3.3 and Secondary Licenses (AGPL not mentioned).

title: Reading AGPL: a guided introduction for first-timers
what_it_supports: AGPL section 13 network copyleft is triggered by modifying the program and supporting remote network interaction; running an unmodified program does not trigger it; the second paragraph bridges GPLv3 and AGPLv3.
